subproblems.title: Countable Lipschitz localization of a C¹ map on an open set (parent step 1(a)–(b))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Z ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be open and let F : ℝ^P → ℝ^n (= Euclid n) be C¹ on Z (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F Z). Then there are open sets V_l ⊆ Z, Borel sets Z_l ⊆ V_l and maps G_l : ℝ^P → ℝ^n (l ∈ ℕ) such that the Z_l are pairwise disjoint, ⋃_l Z_l = Z, every G_l is Lipschitz (LipschitzWith K_l G_l for some K_l ∈ ℝ≥0), and F = G_l on V_l for every l.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Z : Set (Euclid P)) (F : Euclid P → Euclid n), IsOpen Z → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F Z → ∃ (V Zs : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (G : ℕ → Euclid P → Euclid n), (∀ l, IsOpen (V l)) ∧ (∀ l, V l ⊆ Z) ∧ (∀ l, MeasurableSet (Zs l)) ∧ (∀ l, Zs l ⊆ V l) ∧ Pairwise (fun l l' => Disjoint (Zs l) (Zs l')) ∧ (⋃ l, Zs l) = Z ∧ (∀ l, ∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K (G l)) ∧ ∀ l, EqOn F (G l) (V l)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(a)–(b) of the parent proof (Lipschitz localization of F; Simon Ch. 3, §2 works with locally Lipschitz f, chapter-03.txt lines 330–407). Notation: E := ℝ^P, B_ρ(x) and B̄_ρ(x) are the open and the closed ball.
1. (Empty Z.) If Z = ∅, take V_l := ∅, Z_l := ∅ and G_l := 0 (the constant map, 0-Lipschitz) for all l. The empty set is open and Borel, ∅ ⊆ ∅ ⊆ Z, the Z_l are pairwise disjoint, ⋃_l Z_l = ∅ = Z, and F = G_l on V_l = ∅ holds vacuously. From now on Z ≠ ∅.
2. (Local Lipschitz balls.) Let x ∈ Z. Since Z is open there is ε_x > 0 with B_{ε_x}(x) ⊆ Z; put r_x := ε_x/2, so B̄_{r_x}(x) ⊆ B_{ε_x}(x) ⊆ Z. F is C¹ on B̄_{r_x}(x) (ContDiffOn.mono), and B̄_{r_x}(x) is convex and compact (E is proper). By Mathlib ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith (with smoothness order 1 ≠ 0) there is K_x ∈ ℝ≥0 with F K_x-Lipschitz on B̄_{r_x}(x), hence on the open ball B_{r_x}(x).
3. (Countable subcover.) The open balls B_{r_x}(x), x ∈ Z, are contained in Z and cover Z. E is second countable, so by Lindelöf's theorem (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable, applied to the family indexed by the points of Z) there is a countable set D ⊆ Z with ⋃_{x∈D} B_{r_x}(x) = Z. D ≠ ∅ because Z ≠ ∅, so there is a surjection ℕ → D, l ↦ x_l (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range; repetitions allowed). Put V_l := B_{r_{x_l}}(x_l) and K_l := K_{x_l}. Each V_l is open, V_l ⊆ Z, ⋃_l V_l = Z, and F is K_l-Lipschitz on V_l.
4. (Lipschitz extension.) For each l, F is K_l-Lipschitz on V_l and ℝ^n is finite-dimensional, so by Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension there is G_l : E → ℝ^n which is Lipschitz (with constant lipschitzExtensionConstant(ℝ^n)·K_l) and satisfies F = G_l on V_l.
5. (Disjointification.) Put Z_l := V_l ∖ ⋃_{l'<l} V_{l'} (Mathlib disjointed V l). Each Z_l is Borel (a finite Boolean combination of open sets; MeasurableSet.disjointed), Z_l ⊆ V_l, and the Z_l are pairwise disjoint: if l' < l then Z_l ∩ V_{l'} = ∅ while Z_{l'} ⊆ V_{l'} (disjoint_disjointed). Moreover ⋃_l Z_l = ⋃_l V_l = Z: if x lies in some V_l and l is least with this property, then x ∈ Z_l (iUnion_disjointed).
6. (Conclusion.) The families (V_l), (Z_l), (G_l) of steps 3–5 have all the required properties: V_l open, V_l ⊆ Z, Z_l Borel, Z_l ⊆ V_l, Z_l pairwise disjoint, ⋃_l Z_l = Z, G_l Lipschitz, and F = G_l on V_l. ∎
proof_key_steps: Z = ∅: take empty sets and constant maps.
For x ∈ Z pick r_x with B̄_{r_x}(x) ⊆ Z; F is C¹ on this convex compact ball, hence Lipschitz on it (ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith).
Lindelöf: countably many balls V_l = B_{r_{x_l}}(x_l) cover Z (indexed by ℕ with repetitions).
Extend F|V_l to a global Lipschitz map G_l (LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension).
Disjointify: Z_l := V_l ∖ ⋃_{l'<l} V_{l'} are Borel, pairwise disjoint, Z_l ⊆ V_l and ⋃ Z_l = Z.

subproblems.title: C¹ maps on an open set send Hⁿ-null subsets to Lebesgue-null sets (parent step 1(c))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Z ⊆ ℝ^P be open, F : ℝ^P → ℝ^n C¹ on Z (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F Z), and S ⊆ Z with H^n(S) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P. Then L^n(F(S)) = 0, where L^n = volume on ℝ^n = Euclid n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Z S : Set (Euclid P)) (F : Euclid P → Euclid n), IsOpen Z → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F Z → S ⊆ Z → μHE[n] S = 0 → volume (F '' S) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(c) of the parent proof together with its library fact (L1) (Lipschitz images, Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(i); Mathlib/SimonGMT). Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] on E and on ℝ^n; L^n := volume on ℝ^n.
1. (Localization.) By the sibling lipschitz_localization (Submission.idtp_caf_lipschitz_localization) applied to Z and F there are open V_l ⊆ Z, Borel pairwise disjoint Z_l ⊆ V_l with ⋃_l Z_l = Z, and maps G_l : E → ℝ^n, G_l being K_l-Lipschitz for some K_l ∈ ℝ≥0, with F = G_l on V_l (l ∈ ℕ).
2. (Splitting S.) Since S ⊆ Z = ⋃_l Z_l, S = ⋃_l (S ∩ Z_l), hence F(S) = ⋃_l F(S ∩ Z_l). As S ∩ Z_l ⊆ Z_l ⊆ V_l and F = G_l on V_l, F(S ∩ Z_l) = G_l(S ∩ Z_l).
3. (Lipschitz images, (L1).) G_l is K_l-Lipschitz on S ∩ Z_l, so H^n(G_l(S ∩ Z_l)) ≤ K_l^n·H^n(S ∩ Z_l) (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, valid between any two metric spaces with their Borel σ-algebras; equivalently Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le for μH[n] and μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n]). Since H^n(S ∩ Z_l) ≤ H^n(S) = 0, we get H^n(G_l(S ∩ Z_l)) = 0, the measure being μHE[n] on ℝ^n.
4. (Conclusion.) On ℝ^n = Euclid n, μHE[n] = L^n (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so L^n(F(S ∩ Z_l)) = 0 for every l, and by countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null) L^n(F(S)) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take the localization (V_l, Z_l, G_l) of F from the sibling lipschitz_localization.
F(S) = ⋃_l G_l(S ∩ Z_l) since S ⊆ ⋃ Z_l and F = G_l on Z_l ⊆ V_l.
Each G_l(S ∩ Z_l) is μHE[n]-null by the Lipschitz image bound H^n(G(X)) ≤ K^n H^n(X).
μHE[n] = volume on Euclid n and a countable union of null sets is null.

subproblems.title: Disjoint bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces of a countably n-rectifiable Borel set (parent step 2; Simon Ch. 3, 1.2–1.3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable n M). Then there are Lipschitz maps F_i : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, Borel sets B_i ⊆ ℝ^n and constants m_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| for a, a' ∈ B_i, F_i is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B_i, each F_i(B_i) is a Borel subset of M, the sets F_i(B_i) are pairwise disjoint, and H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0 (H^n = μHE[n]).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet M → CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (F : ℕ → Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (m : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ i, ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L (F i)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) ∧ (∀ i, 0 < m i) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, ∀ a' ∈ B i, m i * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F i a - F i a'‖) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, DifferentiableAt ℝ (F i) a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ (F i) a)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (F i '' B i)) ∧ (∀ i, F i '' B i ⊆ M) ∧ Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (F i '' B i) (F j '' B j)) ∧ μHE[n] (M \ ⋃ i, F i '' B i) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the parametrization reduction of Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3, chapter-03.txt lines 25–75, with bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces in place of pieces of C¹ submanifolds). This exact type is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces (candidate commit a2ba78fca36b5fe8a0051278d30da09823c8b59c) and is reused unchanged; the proof below is the argument it formalizes, written with the statement's names F_i, B_i, m_i. Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n]; on ℝ^n, μHE[n] = Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Families are indexed by ℕ and empty pieces are allowed.
1. (Rectifiable cover.) By CountablyRectifiable n M there are M_0 ⊆ E with H^n(M_0) = 0 and Lipschitz maps Φ_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j Φ_j(ℝ^n).
2. (Regular sets.) Let R_j := {a ∈ ℝ^n : Φ_j is differentiable at a and DΦ_j(a) is injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet Φ_j). R_j is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and H^n(Φ_j(ℝ^n ∖ R_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero with s := univ; finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n): the image of the Rademacher-null set of non-differentiability points is null by the Lipschitz image bound, and the image of the critical set is null.
3. (Coercivity constant and radius.) For an injective linear A : ℝ^n → E choose m(A) > 0 with |Ah| ≥ m(A)|h| for all h (m(A) := 1/K for K > 0 with A K-antilipschitz, Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith; this works in every dimension, including n = 0). Put r(A) := m(A)/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise; then r(A) > 0 for every continuous linear A.
4. (Partition.) For each j apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := Φ_j, s := R_j, f' := fderiv ℝ Φ_j (at a ∈ R_j, Φ_j is differentiable, so HasFDerivWithinAt Φ_j (DΦ_j(a)) R_j a) and the radius function r of step 3. It yields pairwise disjoint measurable sets t_{j,k} (k ∈ ℕ) with R_j ⊆ ⋃_k t_{j,k} and continuous linear maps A_{j,k} with |Φ_j(a) − Φ_j(a') − A_{j,k}(a − a')| ≤ r(A_{j,k})|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ R_j ∩ t_{j,k}; moreover, if R_j ≠ ∅, each A_{j,k} equals DΦ_j(y) for some y ∈ R_j.
5. (Bi-Lipschitz pieces.) Put D_{j,k} := R_j ∩ t_{j,k} (Borel) and ρ_{j,k} := r(A_{j,k}) > 0. Then |Φ_j(a) − Φ_j(a')| ≥ ρ_{j,k}|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ D_{j,k}: this is vacuous if D_{j,k} = ∅; otherwise R_j ≠ ∅, so A := A_{j,k} = DΦ_j(y) with y ∈ R_j is injective, ρ_{j,k} = m(A)/2, and |Φ_j(a) − Φ_j(a')| ≥ |A(a − a')| − (m(A)/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m(A)/2)|a − a'|. In particular Φ_j is injective on D_{j,k}, and Φ_j is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of D_{j,k} ⊆ R_j.
6. (Enumeration.) Let i ↦ (j(i), k(i)) be the bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ (Nat.unpair). Put F_i := Φ_{j(i)}, D_i := D_{j(i),k(i)}, m_i := ρ_{j(i),k(i)} > 0 and N_i := F_i(D_i). F_i is continuous, D_i is Borel and F_i is injective on D_i, so N_i is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
7. (Disjoint pieces inside M.) Put B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{−1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}). B_i is Borel (F_i continuous; M and the N_{i'} Borel) and F_i(B_i) = (N_i ∩ M) ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}, which is Borel and contained in M. Since B_i ⊆ D_i, m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| for a, a' ∈ B_i, and F_i is differentiable with injective derivative on B_i; F_i is Lipschitz. If i' < i then F_{i'}(B_{i'}) ⊆ N_{i'} while F_i(B_i) ∩ N_{i'} = ∅, so the F_i(B_i) are pairwise disjoint.
8. (Null remainder.) Let x ∈ M ∖ (M_0 ∪ ⋃_j Φ_j(ℝ^n ∖ R_j)). By step 1, x = Φ_j(a) for some j and a, and a ∈ R_j ⊆ ⋃_k t_{j,k}, so a ∈ D_i for the index i of (j, k) and x ∈ N_i ∩ M. If i_0 is the least index with x ∈ N_{i_0}, then x ∈ F_{i_0}(B_{i_0}). Hence M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i) ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j Φ_j(ℝ^n ∖ R_j), a countable union of H^n-null sets (steps 1–2), and H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
9. (Degenerate dimensions.) No case distinction is needed: for n = 0 every linear map on ℝ^0 is injective and every map ℝ^0 → E is differentiable with injective derivative; if n > P no linear map ℝ^n → E is injective, all R_j are empty, all B_i are empty and step 8 gives H^n(M) = 0. ∎

subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P L-Lipschitz, A ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and c > 0 with c|a − a'| ≤ |g(a) − g(a')| for all a, a' ∈ A, and suppose g is differentiable at every a ∈ A with injective derivative Dg(a) = fderiv ℝ g a. Then for Lebesgue-a.e. a ∈ A (volume.restrict A), g(A) has the approximate tangent space range Dg(a) at g(a) in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (g(A)) (g(a)) (range Dg(a)), i.e. dim range Dg(a) = n and ∫_{η_{g(a),r}(g(A))} f dH^n → ∫_{range Dg(a)} f dH^n as r → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), where η_{y,r}(z) = r^{−1}(z − y) and H^n = μHE[n].

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof, parts (3a), (3d), (3e) and the library facts (L1), (A2), (D), applied to the piece image Γ := g(A) itself (the density argument of Simon's proof of Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 "⇒", chapter-03.txt lines 109–143, with a bi-Lipschitz image in place of a C¹ manifold). Notation: E := ℝ^P; λ := L^n = volume on ℝ^n; H^n := μHE[n] on E and on ℝ^n (on ℝ^n, μHE[n] = λ, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); Λ := L; ω_n := λ(B̄_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞); B_ρ, B̄_ρ open and closed balls; η_{y,r}(z) := r^{−1}(z − y) (SimonGMT blowUpMap y r); J_g(a) := normDet(Dg(a)) (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt g a; Dg(a) := fderiv ℝ g a, the zero map where g is not differentiable); ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f|.
1. (Injectivity and Borel image.) If a, a' ∈ A and g(a) = g(a') then c|a − a'| ≤ 0, so a = a'; thus g is injective on A. As g is continuous and A is Borel in the Polish space ℝ^n, Γ is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
2. (Measure facts.) (a) For S ⊆ ℝ^n, H^n(g(S)) ≤ Λ^n λ(S) (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn and μHE[n] = λ on ℝ^n). (b) For b ∈ A and ρ > 0, Γ ∩ B̄_ρ(g(b)) ⊆ g(A ∩ B̄_{ρ/c}(b)) (if a' ∈ A and |g(a') − g(b)| ≤ ρ then c|a' − b| ≤ ρ), hence H^n(Γ ∩ B̄_ρ(g(b))) ≤ Λ^n ω_n c^{−n} ρ^n < ∞. (c) For y ∈ E, r > 0 and S ⊆ E, H^n(η_{y,r}(S)) = r^{−n}H^n(S) (translation invariance Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and homogeneity Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image); η_{y,r} is a homeomorphism of E, hence a measurable embedding mapping Borel sets to Borel sets, and consequently H^n⌞η_{y,r}(Γ) = r^{−n}·(η_{y,r})_*(H^n⌞Γ) (both sides give H^n(η_{y,r}(Γ) ∩ B') = r^{−n}H^n(Γ ∩ η_{y,r}^{−1}(B')) on Borel B'). (d) J_g is Borel (SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt) and 0 ≤ J_g ≤ Λ^n: ‖Dg(a)‖ ≤ Λ (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz), and for linear T : ℝ^n → E, normDet(T)·ω_n = H^n(T(B̄_1(0))) ≤ ‖T‖^n ω_n (Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume and (a) for the ‖T‖-Lipschitz map T), so normDet(T) ≤ ‖T‖^n. (e) (A2) Injective area formula (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn): for every κ : E → [0, ∞], ∫_Γ κ dH^n = ∫_A J_g(a) κ(g(a)) dλ(a).
3. (Density points, (D).) By the Lebesgue–Besicovitch density theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for λ and A), λ-a.e. b ∈ A is a density point of A: λ(A ∩ B̄_ρ(b))/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺; since λ(B̄_ρ(b)) = ω_nρ^n, equivalently ρ^{−n}λ(B̄_ρ(b) ∖ A) → 0. Claim: if b ∈ A is a density point and v ∈ ℝ^n, there are r_k → 0⁺ and v_k → v with b + r_kv_k ∈ A. For v = 0 take v_k := 0 and r_k := 1/(k + 1). For v ≠ 0 suppose not; then there are ε ∈ (0, |v|) and r_1 > 0 with A ∩ (b + rB_ε(v)) = ∅ for all r ∈ (0, r_1). The set b + rB_ε(v) = B_{rε}(b + rv) is contained in B̄_{r(|v|+ε)}(b) and has λ-measure ω_n(rε)^n (open and closed balls have equal Lebesgue measure because ℝ^n is nontrivial for n ≥ 1, Measure.addHaar_closedBall_eq_addHaar_ball). Hence for ρ := r(|v| + ε) ∈ (0, r_1(|v| + ε)), λ(A ∩ B̄_ρ(b))/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) ≤ 1 − (ε/(|v| + ε))^n, contradicting the density point property.
4. (Lebesgue points.) J_g is bounded and Borel, hence locally integrable, so by the Lebesgue differentiation theorem for the doubling measure λ (Mathlib IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub), for λ-a.e. b: ρ^{−n}∫_{B̄_ρ(b)} |J_g(a) − J_g(b)| dλ(a) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺.
5. (Good parameters.) Let A' be the set of b ∈ A satisfying (α) b is a density point of A (step 3) and (β) the Lebesgue point property of step 4; λ(A ∖ A') = 0. Fix b ∈ A', put y := g(b), L_b := Dg(b) (g is differentiable at b ∈ A), and Φ_r(v) := r^{−1}(g(b + rv) − g(b)) for r > 0. (γ) |L_bv| ≥ c|v| for every v ∈ ℝ^n: by step 3 choose r_k → 0⁺ and v_k → v with b + r_kv_k ∈ A; then c r_k|v_k| ≤ |g(b + r_kv_k) − g(b)| = |r_kL_bv_k + o(r_k)| (differentiability at b, |v_k| bounded); divide by r_k and let k → ∞. Hence L_b is injective, dim range L_b = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj), and L_b is a closed embedding of ℝ^n onto range L_b.
6. (Blow-up representation.) Let f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) and R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0); let r > 0. (i) η_{y,r}(Γ) ∩ B_R(0) = η_{y,r}(Γ ∩ B_{rR}(y)), so by 2(c), 2(b), H^n(η_{y,r}(Γ) ∩ B_R(0)) ≤ r^{−n}Λ^nω_nc^{−n}(rR)^n = Λ^nω_n(R/c)^n < ∞; f is bounded, Borel and zero outside B_R(0), hence H^n-integrable on η_{y,r}(Γ). (ii) By 2(c) (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, integral_smul_measure), ∫_{η_{y,r}(Γ)} f dH^n = r^{−n}∫_Γ f(η_{y,r}(z)) dH^n(z). (iii) Apply 2(e) to κ := ofReal(f∘η_{y,r}) and to κ := ofReal(−f∘η_{y,r}); both sides are finite since κ ≤ ‖f‖_∞·1_{B_{rR}(y)} and H^n(Γ ∩ B_{rR}(y)) < ∞ (2(b)); subtracting (integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part) gives ∫_Γ f(η_{y,r}(z)) dH^n(z) = ∫_A J_g(a) f((g(a) − y)/r) dλ(a). (iv) Substituting a = b + rv (λ is translation invariant and λ(rS) = r^nλ(S); Mathlib integral_comp_smul and integral_add_left_eq_self) yields (*) ∫_{η_{y,r}(Γ)} f dH^n = ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_A(b + rv) J_g(b + rv) f(Φ_r(v)) dλ(v).
7. (Support.) Let D_R := B̄_{R/c}(0) ⊆ ℝ^n. If b + rv ∈ A and f(Φ_r(v)) ≠ 0 then |Φ_r(v)| < R, so c r|v| ≤ |g(b + rv) − g(b)| < rR and |v| < R/c. If f(L_bv) ≠ 0 then |L_bv| < R and |v| < R/c by (γ). So the integrand of (*) and v ↦ J_g(b)f(L_bv) vanish outside D_R, and I_∞ := ∫_{ℝ^n} J_g(b) f(L_bv) dλ(v) = ∫_{D_R} J_g(b) f(L_bv) dλ(v) is finite.
8. (Convergence.) For v ∈ D_R, |1_A(b + rv)J_g(b + rv)f(Φ_r(v)) − J_g(b)f(L_bv)| ≤ Λ^n‖f‖_∞1_{ℝ^n∖A}(b + rv) + ‖f‖_∞|J_g(b + rv) − J_g(b)| + J_g(b)|f(Φ_r(v)) − f(L_bv)| (if b + rv ∉ A the left side is J_g(b)|f(L_bv)| ≤ Λ^n‖f‖_∞; otherwise add and subtract J_g(b)f(Φ_r(v)) and use J_g ≤ Λ^n). Integrating over D_R: the first term gives Λ^n‖f‖_∞ r^{−n}λ(B̄_{rR/c}(b) ∖ A) → 0 by (α) (the set {v ∈ D_R : b + rv ∉ A} is r^{−1}((B̄_{rR/c}(b) ∖ A) − b)); the second gives ‖f‖_∞ r^{−n}∫_{B̄_{rR/c}(b)} |J_g − J_g(b)| dλ → 0 by (β); the third is ≤ J_g(b)λ(D_R) sup_{v∈D_R}|f(Φ_r(v)) − f(L_bv)| → 0, because |Φ_r(v) − L_bv| = r^{−1}|g(b + rv) − g(b) − L_b(rv)| → 0 uniformly for |v| ≤ R/c (differentiability of g at b) and f is uniformly continuous. By (*) and step 7, ∫_{η_{y,r}(Γ)} f dH^n → I_∞ as r → 0⁺.
9. (Identification of the limit.) For every Borel S ⊆ ℝ^n, H^n(L_b(S)) = normDet(L_b)λ(S) = J_g(b)λ(S) (Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume). Hence for Borel B' ⊆ E, H^n(range L_b ∩ B') = H^n(L_b(L_b^{−1}(B'))) = J_g(b)λ(L_b^{−1}(B')), i.e. H^n⌞range L_b = (L_b)_*(J_g(b)·λ), and ∫_{range L_b} f dH^n = J_g(b)∫_{ℝ^n} f(L_bv) dλ(v) = I_∞ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map for the closed embedding L_b, integral_smul_measure).
10. (Conclusion.) For every b ∈ A' (so for λ⌞A-a.e. b): dim range Dg(b) = n (step 5) and ∫_{η_{g(b),r}(Γ)} f dH^n → ∫_{range Dg(b)} f dH^n as r → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) (steps 8–9). This is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (g(A)) (g(b)) (range Dg(b)). ∎
Remark (reuse; not part of the argument). The node ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae of another DAG branch (piece_tangent_density/piece_image_tangent, not yet comparator-accepted when this split was made) has this statement without the hypothesis n ≥ 1 and with the binders renamed (g→F, A→B, c→m), so it is strictly stronger; if it is accepted before this child is formalized, a decomposition of this child may reuse it under its exact name and type. λ-a.e. b ∈ A is a density point of A and a Lebesgue point of J_g; at density points |Dg(b)v| ≥ c|v|, so Dg(b) is injective.
The injective area formula and the substitution a = b + rv give ∫_{η_{g(b),r}(Γ)} f dH^n = ∫ 1_A(b+rv) J_g(b+rv) f(Φ_r(v)) dλ(v), supported in B̄_{R/c}(0).

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of two locally Hⁿ-finite Borel sets agree Hⁿ-a.e. on their overlap (parent steps 3(b), 3(c), 3(f))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^P open, and A, B ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with H^n(A ∩ K) < ∞ and H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W (H^n = μHE[n]). Then for H^n-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P: if x ∈ W, x ∈ A and x ∈ B, then for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (W A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen W → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → μHE[n] (A ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)), x ∈ W → x ∈ A → x ∈ B → ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the locality part of step 3 of the parent proof ((3b) density of the piece in M, (3c) smallness of M ∖ Γ, (3f) comparison of blow-up integrals), stated symmetrically for two sets; Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 (upper density theorem) and Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 86–90 and 113–146). This exact type is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.doraggt_ae_approxTangent_transfer (candidate commit 422e346ed7d2fe5411cb5400351e6936cc4d69fe) and is reused unchanged; the following self-contained proof is the argument it formalizes. Notation: μ := H^n = μHE[n] on E := ℝ^P; for S ⊆ E, x ∈ E and ρ > 0, q_S(x, ρ) := μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)^n ∈ [0, ∞]; η_r := η_{x,r}, η_{x,r}(z) := r^{−1}(z − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r).
1. (Upper density theorem, library fact.) If S ⊆ E is Borel with μ(S) < ∞, then for μ-a.e. x ∉ S, q_S(x, ρ) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺. This is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 (density zero off a set of finite measure), formalized in SimonGMT Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean as simon_theorem_3_6 / ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside for the outer measure of μ, which is Borel regular (SimonGMT Chapter01/Basic.lean measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular) and for which every Borel set is Carathéodory measurable (MeasureTheory.le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory) (upper density limsup_{ρ→0⁺} μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n), exceptional set null for Simon's Hausdorff measure, which is a positive finite multiple of μHE[n], simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_smul_euclideanHausdorffMeasure); since the quotients are ≥ 0, a vanishing upper limit is a limit, and the constant ω_n does not affect a zero limit.
2. (Local version.) Let S ⊆ E be Borel with μ(S ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W. For x ∈ W choose r_x > 0 with B̄_{r_x}(x) ⊆ W. By Lindelöf (E second countable; Mathlib TopologicalSpace.countable_cover_nhdsWithin) there is a countable D ⊆ W with W ⊆ ⋃_{y∈D} B_{r_y}(y). For y ∈ D, S_y := S ∩ B_{r_y}(y) is Borel and μ(S_y) ≤ μ(S ∩ B̄_{r_y}(y)) < ∞ (B̄_{r_y}(y) is a compact subset of W). By step 1 and countability of D, for μ-a.e. x the following holds for every y ∈ D: if x ∉ S_y then q_{S_y}(x, ρ) → 0. Let x be such a point with x ∈ W ∖ S. Choose y ∈ D with x ∈ B_{r_y}(y) and ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ B_{r_y}(y). Then x ∉ S_y, and for 0 < ρ < ε, S_y ∩ B̄_ρ(x) = S ∩ B̄_ρ(x); hence q_S(x, ρ) → 0. Conclusion: for μ-a.e. x, if x ∈ W and x ∉ S then q_S(x, ρ) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺.
3. (Good points.) A ∖ B and B ∖ A are Borel and, being subsets of A resp. B, locally μ-finite in W. Apply step 2 to both: for μ-a.e. x, [x ∈ W, x ∉ A ∖ B ⇒ q_{A∖B}(x, ρ) → 0] and [x ∈ W, x ∉ B ∖ A ⇒ q_{B∖A}(x, ρ) → 0]. Fix such an x with x ∈ W ∩ A ∩ B. Then x ∉ A ∖ B and x ∉ B ∖ A, so q_{A∖B}(x, ρ) → 0 and q_{B∖A}(x, ρ) → 0. Choose r_0 > 0 with B̄_{r_0}(x) ⊆ W; then μ(A ∩ B̄_{r_0}(x)) < ∞ and μ(B ∩ B̄_{r_0}(x)) < ∞.
4. (Reduction.) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q means: finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), ∫_{η_r(S)} f dμ → ∫_Q f dμ as r → 0⁺. The dimension condition is the same for A and B, so it suffices to show, for every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), that Δ(r) := ∫_{η_r(A)} f dμ − ∫_{η_r(B)} f dμ → 0 as r → 0⁺; then the two blow-up integrals converge to the same limits.
5. (Scaling and finiteness.) Fix f; let C_f := sup|f| and R ≥ 1 with f = 0 outside B̄_R(0). For r > 0, η_r is a homeomorphism of E, so it maps Borel sets to Borel sets and η_r(A) ∖ η_r(B) = η_r(A ∖ B), η_r(B) ∖ η_r(A) = η_r(B ∖ A). By translation invariance and homogeneity of μHE[n] (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image), μ(η_r(S) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = r^{−n}μ(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)) = ofReal(R)^n·q_S(x, rR) for every S ⊆ E. For 0 < r < r_0/R this is finite for S ∈ {A, B, A ∖ B, B ∖ A} by step 3.
6. (Comparison.) For 0 < r < r_0/R, f is bounded, Borel and vanishes outside B̄_R(0), so it is μ-integrable on η_r(A) and on η_r(B). Splitting both integrals along the Borel set η_r(A) ∩ η_r(B) gives Δ(r) = ∫_{η_r(A∖B)} f dμ − ∫_{η_r(B∖A)} f dμ, hence |Δ(r)| ≤ C_f·ofReal(R)^n·(q_{A∖B}(x, rR) + q_{B∖A}(x, rR)) (as real numbers), which tends to 0 as r → 0⁺ by step 3.
7. (Conclusion.) By steps 4–6, at every point x of step 3 (μ-a.e.) with x ∈ W ∩ A ∩ B, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q for every Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Upper density theorem (Simon 1.3.6): a Borel set of finite H^n measure has H^n-density 0 at H^n-a.e. point outside it.
Localize with a countable cover of W by balls with compact closure in W to get density zero of S at a.e. x ∈ W ∖ S.
At a.e. x ∈ W ∩ A ∩ B both A∖B and B∖A have density zero, and A, B have finite measure near x.
Blow-up scaling: |∫_{η_r(A)} f − ∫_{η_r(B)} f| ≤ sup|f| R^n (q_{A∖B}(x,rR) + q_{B∖A}(x,rR)) → 0, so the approximate tangent conditions coincide.

subproblems.title: Borel image of a bi-Lipschitz piece and pull-back of Hⁿ-a.e. properties to the parameters (parent step 3(a))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and m > 0 with m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for all a, a' ∈ B. Then F(B) is Borel, and for every predicate p on ℝ^P that holds H^n⌞F(B)-a.e. (H^n = μHE[n]), p(F(b)) holds for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B (volume.restrict B).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (L : NNReal) (m : ℝ), LipschitzWith L F → MeasurableSet B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, m * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F a - F a'‖) → MeasurableSet (F '' B) ∧ ∀ p : Euclid P → Prop, (∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n].restrict (F '' B)), p y) → ∀ᵐ b ∂(volume.restrict B), p (F b)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3(a) of the parent proof (the inverse of g_i on its piece is c_i^{−1}-Lipschitz, so H^n-null subsets of the piece image pull back to Lebesgue-null parameter sets) and the Lusin–Souslin theorem used in its step 2(f). This exact type is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.ptd_piece_image_measurable_ae_pullback (candidate commit bed5b8494a351297a2be8f0a0b63079868d53507) and is reused unchanged; the proof below is the argument it formalizes. Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] on E and on ℝ^n; λ := volume on ℝ^n; on ℝ^n, μHE[n] = λ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. (Injectivity.) F is injective on B: if a, a' ∈ B and F(a) = F(a') then m|a − a'| ≤ 0, and m > 0 gives a = a'.
2. (Borel image.) F is continuous (Lipschitz), ℝ^n is Polish, B is Borel and F is injective on B, so F(B) is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
3. (Inverse map.) Let Ginv := Function.invFunOn F B : E → ℝ^n. For y ∈ F(B), Ginv(y) ∈ B and F(Ginv(y)) = y (invFunOn_pos). For y, y' ∈ F(B), m|Ginv(y) − Ginv(y')| ≤ |F(Ginv(y)) − F(Ginv(y'))| = |y − y'|, so Ginv is m^{−1}-Lipschitz on F(B). By the Lipschitz image bound (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn), μHE[n](Ginv(S)) ≤ (m^{−1})^n·μHE[n](S) for every S ⊆ F(B).
4. (Pull-back.) Let p hold H^n⌞F(B)-a.e. Since F(B) is measurable (step 2), ae_restrict_iff' shows that S := {y : y ∈ F(B) ∧ ¬p(y)} is H^n-null. Let T := {b ∈ B : ¬p(F(b))}. If b ∈ T then y := F(b) ∈ S, Ginv(y) ∈ B and F(Ginv(y)) = F(b), so Ginv(y) = b by step 1; hence T ⊆ Ginv(S). By step 3 and μHE[n] = λ on ℝ^n, λ(T) ≤ μHE[n](Ginv(S)) ≤ (m^{−1})^n·0 = 0. Since B is measurable, ae_restrict_iff' turns λ(T) = 0 into: p(F(b)) holds for (volume.restrict B)-a.e. b. For n = 0 every power equals 1 and the argument is unchanged. ∎
proof_key_steps: The lower bound makes F injective on B.
Lusin–Souslin: F(B) is Borel.
invFunOn F B is m^{-1}-Lipschitz on F(B), so it maps H^n-null subsets of F(B) to λ-null sets.
The bad parameters {b ∈ B : ¬p(F b)} lie in the inverse image of the H^n-null bad set, hence are λ-null.

subproblems.title: The contract's chosen approximate tangent plane equals any approximate tangent space (parent step 3, 'consequently')
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary, x ∈ ℝ^P and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P. If HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4), then approxTangentPlane n M x = Q, where approxTangentPlane n M x is the contract's choice (a chosen plane with the property if one exists, ⊥ otherwise).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → approxTangentPlane n M x = Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the "consequently" clause of step 3 of the parent proof (approxTangentPlane n M x is a chosen Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q whenever one exists, and any two such Q coincide), i.e. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1). This exact type is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dpf_itt_approxTangentPlane_eq (candidate commit 34325ececca5ed226212e37aa67e711a3a090e9d) and is reused unchanged; the proof below is the argument it formalizes.
1. (Definition.) In GMT/Ch07/Contract.lean, approxTangentPlane n M x is defined classically as h.choose if h : ∃ Q', HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q' holds, and as ⊥ otherwise.
2. (The condition holds.) From hQ : HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q we get h := ⟨Q, hQ⟩, so the positive branch of the dependent if-then-else is taken (dite_eq_left / dif_pos) and approxTangentPlane n M x = h.choose.
3. (Chosen plane.) By Exists.choose_spec, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x h.choose.
4. (Uniqueness.) SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1)) states that HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₁ and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₂ imply Q₁ = Q₂ (the limits ∫_{Q₁} f dH^n and ∫_{Q₂} f dH^n of the same blow-up integrals coincide for every f ∈ C_c, so H^n⌞Q₁ = H^n⌞Q₂ as regular measures, and the support of H^n⌞Q_k is Q_k because dim Q_k = n). Applied to steps 3 and hQ it gives h.choose = Q.
5. By steps 2 and 4, approxTangentPlane n M x = Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: The hypothesis witnesses the existential in the definition, so approxTangentPlane n M x = h.choose.
h.choose is an approximate tangent plane (Exists.choose_spec).
Uniqueness of approximate tangent planes (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) gives h.choose = Q.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of the carrier along a bi-Lipschitz piece (parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P (H^n = μHE[n]), g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P L-Lipschitz, A ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and c > 0 with c|a − a'| ≤ |g(a) − g(a')| for a, a' ∈ A, g differentiable with injective derivative Dg(a) = fderiv ℝ g a at every a ∈ A, and g(A) ⊆ M. Then approxTangentPlane n M (g(a)) = range Dg(a) for Lebesgue-a.e. a ∈ A (volume.restrict A).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (L : NNReal) (c : ℝ), 1 ≤ n → MeasurableSet M → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μHE[n] (M ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → LipschitzWith L g → MeasurableSet A → 0 < c → (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ a' ∈ A, c * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖g a - g a'‖) → (∀ a ∈ A, DifferentiableAt ℝ g a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ g a)) → g '' A ⊆ M → ∀ᵐ a ∂(volume.restrict A), approxTangentPlane n M (g a) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ g a : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof ("For every i and L^n-a.e. a ∈ A_i, M has the approximate tangent space range Dg_i(a) at g_i(a); consequently T_{g_i(a)} = range Dg_i(a)"). Its four ingredients are the siblings: piece_image_tangent (parts (3a), (3d), (3e): the tangent plane of the piece itself), tangent_transfer (parts (3b), (3c), (3f): locality of approximate tangent planes), piece_pullback (part (3a): H^n-a.e. statements on the piece pull back to the parameters) and chosen_plane (the "consequently" clause). Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n]; λ := volume on ℝ^n; Γ := g(A).
1. (Piece image.) By the sibling piece_pullback (Submission.ptd_piece_image_measurable_ae_pullback) applied to g, A, L, c: Γ is Borel, and every property of points of E holding H^n⌞Γ-a.e. holds at g(a) for λ⌞A-a.e. a.
2. (Local finiteness of Γ.) Γ ⊆ M, so H^n(Γ ∩ K) ≤ H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ E.
3. (Locality.) The sibling tangent_transfer (Submission.doraggt_ae_approxTangent_transfer) with W := E (open), A := Γ and B := M (both Borel, and locally H^n-finite on compact sets by step 2 and the hypothesis) gives: for H^n-a.e. x, if x ∈ Γ (then also x ∈ M) then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Γ x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q for every subspace Q. As Γ is Borel, this says (ae_restrict_iff') that the property "∀ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Γ x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q" holds for H^n⌞Γ-a.e. x.
4. (Pull-back.) By steps 1 and 3, for λ⌞A-a.e. a: for every Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Γ (g(a)) Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (g(a)) Q.
5. (Tangent plane of the piece.) By the sibling piece_image_tangent (Submission.idtp_caf_piece_image_approxTangent_ae; hypotheses n ≥ 1, g L-Lipschitz, A Borel, c > 0, the lower bound, differentiability with injective derivative on A), for λ⌞A-a.e. a: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Γ (g(a)) (range Dg(a)).
6. (Conclusion.) For λ⌞A-a.e. a both step 4 and step 5 hold (intersection of two conull sets); then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (g(a)) (range Dg(a)) by step 4 with Q := range Dg(a), and the sibling chosen_plane (Submission.dpf_itt_approxTangentPlane_eq) gives approxTangentPlane n M (g(a)) = range Dg(a). ∎
proof_key_steps: piece_pullback: g(A) is Borel and H^n⌞g(A)-a.e. properties hold at g(a) for a.e. a ∈ A.
g(A) ⊆ M is locally H^n-finite; tangent_transfer with W = ℝ^P makes the approximate tangent planes of g(A) and M agree H^n⌞g(A)-a.e.
Pull back this agreement to a.e. parameter a ∈ A.
piece_image_tangent: g(A) has approximate tangent space range Dg(a) at g(a) for a.e. a.
Hence M has approximate tangent space range Dg(a) at g(a), and chosen_plane identifies approxTangentPlane n M (g a).

subproblems.title: Weighted fibre-sum area formula on one bi-Lipschitz piece for a locally Lipschitz map into ℝ^n (parent steps 0, 5, 6, 7 on a piece)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ; g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P Lipschitz; A ⊆ ℝ^n Borel with g injective on A and differentiable at every point of A; V ⊆ ℝ^P open with g(A) ⊆ V; G : ℝ^P → ℝ^n Lipschitz; F : ℝ^P → ℝ^n with F = G on V and F differentiable at every point of g(A); T : ℝ^P → {linear subspaces of ℝ^P} with T(g(a)) = range Dg(a) for Lebesgue-a.e. a ∈ A (Dg(a) = fderiv ℝ g a); and h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] a.e. measurable for H^n⌞g(A) (H^n = μHE[n]). For x ∈ ℝ^P let J_T(x) := (det(⟨DF(x)u_i, DF(x)u_j⟩)_{i,j})^{1/2}, where DF(x) = fderiv ℝ F x and (u_i) is the standard orthonormal basis (stdOrthonormalBasis) of T(x), indexed by Fin(dim T(x)). Then the fibre-sum function y ↦ Σ_{x ∈ g(A), F(x) = y} h(x) (the tsum over the subtype g(A) ∩ F^{−1}{y}) is a.e. measurable for Lebesgue measure L^n (volume) on ℝ^n, and ∫_{ℝ^n} Σ_{x ∈ g(A), F(x) = y} h(x) dL^n(y) = ∫_{g(A)} J_T(x)·h(x) dH^n(x), the factor J_T entering through ENNReal.ofReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (Lg : NNReal) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (F G : Euclid P → Euclid n) (LG : NNReal) (T : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (h : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞), LipschitzWith Lg g → MeasurableSet A → InjOn g A → (∀ a ∈ A, DifferentiableAt ℝ g a) → IsOpen V → g '' A ⊆ V → LipschitzWith LG G → EqOn F G V → (∀ x ∈ g '' A, DifferentiableAt ℝ F x) → (∀ᵐ a ∂(volume.restrict A), T (g a) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ g a : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)) → AEMeasurable h (μHE[n].restrict (g '' A)) → AEMeasurable (fun y : Euclid n => ∑' x : ↥(g '' A ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) volume ∧ ∫⁻ y, (∑' x : ↥(g '' A ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) ∂volume = ∫⁻ x in g '' A, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ (T x)) => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ F x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (T x) i)) (fderiv ℝ F x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (T x) j))))) * h x ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0, 5, 6 and 7 of the parent proof restricted to one piece S = g(A) (Simon Ch. 3, §2, (2.4)–(2.5), chapter-03.txt lines 330–407, proved there by applying the Euclidean area formula of Ch. 2, 3.4–3.5 piece by piece), with the library facts (L1), (A1), (A2), (G). Notation: E := ℝ^P; λ := L^n = volume on ℝ^n; H^n := μHE[n] on E and on ℝ^n (on ℝ^n, μHE[n] = λ, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); Γ := g(A); Φ := G∘g : ℝ^n → ℝ^n, which is Lipschitz; for φ between finite-dimensional inner product spaces, Dφ(a) := fderiv ℝ φ a and J_φ(a) := normDet(Dφ(a)) ≥ 0 (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt φ a, Mathlib LinearMap.normDet); for k : E → [0, ∞] and y ∈ ℝ^n, Σ_k(y) := Σ_{x∈Γ, F(x)=y} k(x) ∈ [0, ∞] (tsum over the subtype Γ ∩ F^{−1}{y}).
Library facts. (L1) If ψ is K-Lipschitz on X then μHE[n](ψ(X)) ≤ K^n μHE[n](X) (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). (A1) For a Lipschitz φ : ℝ^n → ℝ^n, a Borel s ⊆ ℝ^n and a Borel w : ℝ^n → [0, ∞], the fibre sum y ↦ Σ_{a∈s, φ(a)=y} w(a) is μHE[n]-a.e. measurable and ∫ Σ_{a∈s, φ(a)=y} w(a) dμHE[n](y) = ∫_s J_φ(a)w(a) dλ(a) (SimonGMT Chapter02/AreaNoninjective.lean aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitz and weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_fiberSum; finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n). (A2) For a Lipschitz ψ : ℝ^n → E, a Borel s on which ψ is injective and an arbitrary κ : E → [0, ∞], ∫_{ψ(s)} κ dμHE[n] = ∫_s J_ψ(a)κ(ψ(a)) dλ(a) (SimonGMT Chapter02/AreaLipschitz.lean weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn). (G) For linear L : ℝ^n → E and A' : E → ℝ^n, normDet(A'∘L) = normDet(A'|_{range L})·normDet(L) (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_comp), and for a subspace T ⊆ E with orthonormal basis u, normDet(A'|_T)² = det(⟨A'u_i, A'u_j⟩)_{i,j} (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram applied to A'.domRestrict T and u; Matrix.gram is the matrix of inner products).
1. (Γ is Borel.) g is continuous, A is Borel in the Polish space ℝ^n and g is injective on A, so Γ is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
2. (Reduction to Borel h; parent step 0.) As h is a.e. measurable for H^n⌞Γ, there is a Borel h̃ : E → [0, ∞] with (H^n⌞Γ)({h ≠ h̃}) = 0; since Γ is Borel, Measure.restrict_apply' gives H^n(N) = 0 for N := Γ ∩ {h ≠ h̃}. As N ⊆ Γ ⊆ V and F = G on V, F(N) = G(N), and by (L1) for the Lipschitz G, H^n(G(N)) = 0 on ℝ^n, i.e. λ(F(N)) = 0. If y ∉ F(N), every x ∈ Γ with F(x) = y satisfies h(x) = h̃(x), so Σ_h(y) = Σ_{h̃}(y); hence Σ_h = Σ_{h̃} λ-a.e. Also J_T·h = J_T·h̃ H^n⌞Γ-a.e. Since a.e. measurability is preserved by a.e. equality and lintegrals of a.e. equal functions coincide, both conclusions for h follow from those for h̃. From now on h is Borel.
3. (Fibres; parent step 7 on the piece.) Fix y ∈ ℝ^n. The map a ↦ g(a) is a bijection from {a ∈ A : Φ(a) = y} onto {x ∈ Γ : F(x) = y}: if a ∈ A and Φ(a) = y, then g(a) ∈ Γ ⊆ V, so F(g(a)) = G(g(a)) = y; if x ∈ Γ and F(x) = y, then x = g(a) for some a ∈ A and Φ(a) = G(g(a)) = F(g(a)) = y (F = G on V ∋ x); and g is injective on A. Reindexing the [0, ∞]-valued sum along this bijection (Equiv.tsum_eq) gives Σ_h(y) = W(y) := Σ_{a∈A, Φ(a)=y} h(g(a)).
4. (Euclidean area formula (A1).) Φ is Lipschitz, A is Borel and w := h∘g is Borel (h Borel, g continuous). By (A1) and μHE[n] = λ on ℝ^n, W is λ-a.e. measurable and ∫ W dλ = ∫_A J_Φ(a)h(g(a)) dλ(a). By step 3, Σ_h = W, so Σ_h is λ-a.e. measurable and ∫ Σ_h dλ = ∫_A J_Φ(a)h(g(a)) dλ(a).
5. (Jacobian chain rule; parent step 5.) Let a ∈ A with T(g(a)) = range Dg(a); by hypothesis this holds for λ⌞A-a.e. a. Put x := g(a) ∈ Γ ⊆ V, L := Dg(a) (g is differentiable at a ∈ A) and A' := DF(x) (F is differentiable at x ∈ Γ). Since F = G on the open set V ∋ x, F and G agree on a neighbourhood of x, so G is differentiable at x with DG(x) = A' (HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq, Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). By the chain rule Φ = G∘g is differentiable at a and DΦ(a) = A'∘L. By (G), J_Φ(a) = normDet(A'∘L) = normDet(A'|_{range L})·normDet(L) = normDet(A'|_{T(x)})·J_g(a), and normDet(A'|_{T(x)})² = det(⟨A'u_i, A'u_j⟩)_{i,j} for the standard orthonormal basis u of T(x); as normDet ≥ 0, normDet(A'|_{T(x)}) = J_T(x). Hence J_Φ(a) = J_T(g(a))·J_g(a) for λ⌞A-a.e. a.
6. (Carrier side; parent step 6 on the piece.) Apply (A2) to ψ := g, s := A (g is Lipschitz and injective on the Borel set A) and κ := ofReal(J_T)·h (no measurability of κ is needed): ∫_Γ ofReal(J_T)h dH^n = ∫_A ofReal(J_g(a))·ofReal(J_T(g(a)))·h(g(a)) dλ(a). By step 5 and ofReal(st) = ofReal(s)ofReal(t) for s, t ≥ 0, the integrand equals ofReal(J_Φ(a))·h(g(a)) for λ⌞A-a.e. a, so ∫_Γ ofReal(J_T)h dH^n = ∫_A J_Φ(a)h(g(a)) dλ(a).
7. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 6, Σ_h is λ-a.e. measurable and ∫ Σ_h dλ = ∫_A J_Φ(a)h(g(a)) dλ(a) = ∫_Γ ofReal(J_T)·h dH^n, which are the two assertions (for Borel h, hence, by step 2, for the given h). ∎
proof_key_steps: g(A) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin); replace h by a Borel h̃ equal to it H^n-a.e. on g(A): the exceptional set N is H^n-null and F(N) = G(N) is λ-null since G is Lipschitz.
For each y, a ↦ g(a) is a bijection {a ∈ A : G(g(a)) = y} → {x ∈ g(A) : F(x) = y}, so the carrier fibre sum equals the parameter fibre sum of Φ = G∘g with weight h∘g.
The Euclidean weighted area formula for the Lipschitz Φ gives a.e. measurability and ∫ fibre sum = ∫_A J_Φ · h∘g dλ.
Where T(g(a)) = range Dg(a): DΦ(a) = DF(g(a))∘Dg(a) (F = G near g(a)), and normDet_comp + normDet_sq_eq_det_gram give J_Φ(a) = J_T(g(a))·J_g(a).
The injective area formula for g with the arbitrary weight J_T·h gives ∫_{g(A)} J_T h dH^n = ∫_A J_g·J_T∘g·h∘g dλ = ∫_A J_Φ · h∘g dλ.

subproblems.title: Gluing the fibre-sum area formula over a countable disjoint Borel partition modulo a null set (parent steps 6–7, summation)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, ι a countable type, S ⊆ ℝ^P, and S_k ⊆ S (k ∈ ι) pairwise disjoint Borel sets; let F : ℝ^P → ℝ^n and φ, h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] be arbitrary. Assume H^n(S ∖ ⋃_k S_k) = 0 (H^n = μHE[n]) and L^n(F(S ∖ ⋃_k S_k)) = 0 (L^n = volume on ℝ^n), and that for every k the fibre-sum function y ↦ Σ_{x ∈ S_k, F(x) = y} h(x) (tsum over the subtype S_k ∩ F^{−1}{y}) is L^n-a.e. measurable with ∫ Σ_{x ∈ S_k, F(x) = y} h(x) dL^n(y) = ∫_{S_k} φ·h dH^n. Then y ↦ Σ_{x ∈ S, F(x) = y} h(x) is L^n-a.e. measurable and ∫ Σ_{x ∈ S, F(x) = y} h(x) dL^n(y) = ∫_S φ·h dH^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ι : Type) [Countable ι] (S : Set (Euclid P)) (pieces : ι → Set (Euclid P)) (F : Euclid P → Euclid n) (φ h : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞), (∀ k, MeasurableSet (pieces k)) → (∀ k, pieces k ⊆ S) → Pairwise (fun k k' => Disjoint (pieces k) (pieces k')) → μHE[n] (S \ ⋃ k, pieces k) = 0 → volume (F '' (S \ ⋃ k, pieces k)) = 0 → (∀ k, AEMeasurable (fun y : Euclid n => ∑' x : ↥(pieces k ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) volume ∧ ∫⁻ y, (∑' x : ↥(pieces k ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) ∂volume = ∫⁻ x in pieces k, φ x * h x ∂μHE[n]) → AEMeasurable (fun y : Euclid n => ∑' x : ↥(S ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) volume ∧ ∫⁻ y, (∑' x : ↥(S ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) ∂volume = ∫⁻ x in S, φ x * h x ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the summation parts of steps 6 and 7 of the parent proof (M ∩ Z is the disjoint union of the H^n-null set N_0 and the Borel pieces S_{i,l}; restrict_iUnion, lintegral_sum_measure, the splitting of the fibre sum along the disjoint decomposition, the null set F(N_0), AEMeasurable.ennreal_tsum and lintegral_tsum). Notation: μ := H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P; λ := L^n = volume on ℝ^n; U := ⋃_k S_k; N := S ∖ U; for X ⊆ ℝ^P and y ∈ ℝ^n, Σ_X(y) := Σ_{x ∈ X ∩ F^{−1}{y}} h(x) ∈ [0, ∞].
1. (Carrier side.) U ⊆ S (each S_k ⊆ S) and S ∖ U = N is μ-null, so S and U are μ-a.e. equal and μ⌞S = μ⌞U (Measure.restrict_congr_set). The S_k are Borel and pairwise disjoint and ι is countable, so μ⌞U = Σ_k μ⌞S_k (Measure.restrict_iUnion). The lintegral of any [0, ∞]-valued function against a sum of measures is the sum of the lintegrals (lintegral_sum_measure, no measurability needed). Hence ∫_S φh dμ = Σ_k ∫_{S_k} φh dμ.
2. (Fibre decomposition.) Let y ∉ F(N). Then S ∩ F^{−1}{y} = ⋃_k (S_k ∩ F^{−1}{y}): "⊇" because S_k ⊆ S; "⊆" because an x ∈ S with F(x) = y cannot lie in N (else y ∈ F(N)), so x ∈ S_k for some k. The sets S_k ∩ F^{−1}{y} are pairwise disjoint, so the subtype of the union is in bijection with the dependent sum Σ_k (S_k ∩ F^{−1}{y}) (Set.unionEqSigmaOfDisjoint) and the [0, ∞]-valued sum splits: Σ_S(y) = Σ_k Σ_{S_k}(y) (Equiv.tsum_eq, ENNReal.tsum_sigma'). Since λ(F(N)) = 0, Σ_S = Σ_k Σ_{S_k} λ-a.e.
3. (Measurability.) Each Σ_{S_k} is λ-a.e. measurable by hypothesis, so y ↦ Σ_k Σ_{S_k}(y) is λ-a.e. measurable (AEMeasurable.ennreal_tsum, ι countable), and so is the a.e. equal function Σ_S (AEMeasurable.congr).
4. (Integral.) ∫ Σ_S dλ = ∫ Σ_k Σ_{S_k} dλ (lintegral_congr_ae, step 2) = Σ_k ∫ Σ_{S_k} dλ (lintegral_tsum, using step 3's a.e. measurability of each term) = Σ_k ∫_{S_k} φh dμ (hypothesis) = ∫_S φh dμ (step 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: μ⌞S = μ⌞⋃S_k = Σ_k μ⌞S_k (null remainder, restrict_iUnion), so ∫_S φh dμ = Σ_k ∫_{S_k} φh dμ for any φh.
Off the λ-null set F(S ∖ ⋃S_k) the fibre of S over y is the disjoint union of the fibres of the S_k, so the fibre sum over S is Σ_k of the fibre sums over S_k.
A countable sum of a.e. measurable [0,∞]-valued functions is a.e. measurable; so is the a.e. equal fibre sum over S.
lintegral_tsum and the per-piece hypothesis give ∫ fibre sum over S = Σ_k ∫_{S_k} φh dμ = ∫_S φh dμ.
